subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw add explicit `first-progress` and `startup-failed` lifecycle phases for sub-agent startup, or solve silent startup aborts through the existing terminal lifecycle states?
rationale: The observable bug is real at source level, but the proposed fix creates a core event contract that crosses gateway/session/SDK/subagent consumers and the existing PR is not a safe landing branch.

options.title: Add explicit startup lifecycle phases
options.body: Implement `first-progress` and `startup-failed` on current main across the active embedded-agent, subagent, gateway, session, SDK, docs, and tests surfaces.

options.title: Stay within existing terminal phases
options.body: Map startup aborts into an existing error/killed terminal state with visible diagnostics and avoid adding a new lifecycle phase contract.

options.title: Defer the contract
options.body: Keep the issue open as the canonical design item until a maintainer sponsors the lifecycle API shape and proof requirements.

recommendation.title: Add explicit startup lifecycle phases
recommendation.body: Implement `first-progress` and `startup-failed` on current main across the active embedded-agent, subagent, gateway, session, SDK, docs, and tests surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest history across subagent lifecycle stabilization and the current registry/session lifecycle surfaces affected by the decision.
